newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP halts zloty rise, pulls up 1-day rates.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP halts zloty rise, pulls up 1-day rates.

text.p: The Polish central bank bought some $50-60 million to punish the stubborn zloty after catching the local unit wondering above the safe confines of 2.5 percent from parity, which dealers said was the new resistance level.
They said the zloty was propelled by domestic banks cutting long currency positions to keep higher yielding zloty deposits over the weekend.

"There was no visible foreign involvement today and the currency selling is likely to have come from banks cutting long positions for the weeked," said Karol Zaluski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

The zloty closed at 2.51/2.47 percent from the trading band centre, stronger than Tuesday's close at 2.41/2.37. It was at 3.1415/25 to the dollar, down from 3.1340/50 on Tuesday and at 1.8320/28 to the mark, up from 1.8360/70.
On the money market the NBP lifted tomorrow/next rates by one point to 20.50/21.50 with a 788 million zloty drainage with a T/N value date at a flat maximum rate of 22.15 percent.

It boosted overnight rates also by one point to 19.70/21.10 with a 255 million zloty sale of its 91-day bills with an O/N value date. The average accepted yield rose to 22.19 percent from Tuesday's 22.13 percent.
